In binding/multipart_form_mapping.go, setByMultipartFormFile ends with a default `return false, ErrMultiFileHeader` (the package-level sentinel errors.New("unsupported field type for multipart.FileHeader")). So when value.Kind() is not Ptr, Struct, Slice or Array, it returns (false, ErrMultiFileHeader) — i.e. isSet == false and a non-nil error.
errors.go (#1): fix is being applied and verified now (Unwrap receiver changed to value receiver so a gin.Error value unwraps too). ETA ~4 min.

Mode() returns the package-level `modeName` string — the currently active gin mode name. It is initialised to DebugMode ("debug") and is only changed by SetMode; e.g. after SetMode(TestMode) it returns "test".

defaultHandleRecovery(c *Context, err any) simply calls c.AbortWithStatus(http.StatusInternalServerError) — it aborts the handler chain with HTTP 500 and writes no body of its own (the status line/headers are flushed by the abort). It is the default RecoveryFunc used by Recovery()/RecoveryWithWriter() when no custom handler is supplied.
context.go (#15, TestContextNegotiationFormat2): investigating the content-negotiation logic now; ETA ~8 min.

defaultValidator.lazyinit() calls v.validate.SetTagName("binding") — the tag name is the string "binding" (so struct fields are validated via their `binding:"..."` tags, not the validator's default `validate` tag).

SecureJSON.Render writes r.Prefix only when the marshaled data is a JSON array, i.e. when both:

    bytes.HasPrefix(jsonBytes, []byte("[")) && bytes.HasSuffix(jsonBytes, []byte("]"))

If that holds it writes r.Prefix first (returning immediately if that write errors), then always writes jsonBytes.

When the `time_format` tag is empty, setTimeField uses `time.RFC3339`, i.e. the layout "2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00" (binding/form_mapping.go: `timeFormat := structField.Tag.Get("time_format"); if timeFormat == "" { timeFormat = time.RFC3339 }`). That single layout is then passed to time.ParseInLocation; the only other special cases are the whole-tag values "unix"/"unixnano" (case-insensitive), which are parsed as epoch seconds/nanoseconds.

It returns nil immediately: `if obj == nil { return nil }` is the first statement of defaultValidator.ValidateStruct, so a nil object is treated as valid (no error, and the validator is not even lazily initialised).

Still working: the injected-defect fixes for response_writer.go (#4), tree.go (#8/#11), context.go (#15/#18) are being applied and verified by running subagents; final verification of the full `go test ./...` suite is pending. errors.go (#1) is already fixed and verified.
